subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The coelacanth is a fish species.
• Up until 1938, it was believed to be extinct.
• That year, a live coelacanth was caught off the coast of South Africa.
• The coelacanth is considered a living fossil.
• "Living fossil" is a term for organisms that have remained essentially unchanged for millions of years and were thought to be extinct.
prompt: The student wants to define the term "living fossil" and provide an example of one. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish these goals?

choices.A: The term "living fossil" describes an organism, such as the coelacanth, that has remained essentially unchanged for millions of years and was thought to be extinct.
choices.B: One example of a living fossil is the coelacanth, a fish species that was caught off the coast of South Africa in 1938.
choices.C: The coelacanth, a species of fish, was caught off the coast of South Africa in 1938.
choices.D: Sometimes, an organism that has remained unchanged for millions of years is later discovered to still exist.

explanation:
Choice A is correct. It defines 'living fossil' as an organism unchanged for millions of years thought extinct, providing the coelacanth as an example.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The sentence provides information about the coelacanth; it doesn't define the term "living fossil" or explicitly identify the coelacanth as a living fossil.
